description.narrative: Samarbetet är ett icke öronmärkt stöd till Civic Resistance/ CR/Qëndresa Qytetare och baseras på partnerns strategiska plan 2024-2027. Genom att stärka ungdomars kapacitet, vilket är ett av huvudmålen i den strategiska planen, avser partnern att fungera som en vakthund för offentliga utgifter till universitet och bli en kritisk röst för ungdomar när det gäller utmaningar inom högre utbildning i Albanien. Initiativ inom ramen för den strategiska planen för CR inkluderar övervakning av nationella strategier och resultat för institutioner på central och lokal nivå, organisation av utbildningsakademier för val, rättvisa och medborgarnas deltagande i beslutsfattande, framställningar, kreativa former av protester och medborgarengagemang, kapacitetsuppbyggnad av unga ledare, etc.

The cooperation is un-earmarked support to Civic Resistance/ CR/Qëndresa Qytetare and is based on the partner’s Strategic Plan 2024-2027. Through strengthening the capacities of young people, which is one of the main goals of the strategic plan, the partner intend to act as a watchdog to public spending to universities and become a critical voice of the youth concerning higher education challenges in Albania. Initiatives under the Strategic Plan of CR include various monitoring of national strategies and performance for institutions at central and local level, organization of education academies on election, justice, and citizens participation in decision making, petitions, creative forms of protest and citizen’s engagement, capacity building of young leaders, etc.

The Strategic Plan of Civic Resistance/Qëndresa Qytetare has five strategic objectives:
Strategic Objective 1 - Promotion of Improved Educational Services Strategic Objective 2 - Encouraging the participation of citizens in democratic processes Strategic Objective 3 - Strengthening Institutional Capacity via Good Governance Strategic Objective 4 - Networking and Collaboration Strategic Objective 5 - Partnership for Environmental Sustainability

description.narrative:
During 2024, Civic Resistance (Qëndresa Qytetare/QQ) has made good progress to achieving the five strategic outcomes. Examples for each outcome area are presented below:
Outcome 1: Implement an evidence-based advocacy agenda developed with the help of members and organizations with similar goals.
- The most visible outcome of this evidence-based advocacy work is in the field of education. The Monitoring Report on the Education Strategy demonstrates the potential for influence with regards to monitoring related activities. The report became a key reference point in the public debate during November and December 2024, addressing safety and quality of education. The report served as the foundation for the demands of five parent-led protests and discussions with the Parliamentary Committee on Education, which held a hearing with the Minister of Education based on its findings.
- Advocacy work and research on the participation of public officials in election campaigns. The findings were followed by the Electoral Commission.
- Issuing 30 public statements addressing critical issues on education and human rights and calling on the relevant authorities to address them.
Outcome 2: Encouraging the participation of citizens in democratic processes.
- One of the key achievements during 2024 was the Democratic Education Academies, with the participation of 100 young individuals, 62 girls and 38 boys, from across Albania, including regions such as Kukës, Shkodër, Tropojë, and Dibër. The participants gained valuable tools for active participation, which they used to create 5 (five) creative activism initiatives aimed at addressing local governance issues. These initiatives have already resulted in tangible outcomes, including influencing local policy decisions and driving greater community involvement in governance.
- Three petitions, gathering a combined total of 697 signatures, have directly influenced local policy decisions, showcasing the power of citizens to demand accountability and action from their local authorities. As a result: In Shkodra, construction began on Albanias first student cafeteria, easing the financial burden on students in the city. In Pogradec, following a youth-led petition, the Municipal Council allocated funding for bicycle lanes, set to be completed in 2025, improving urban mobility and sustainability.
Outcome 3: Strengthening Institutional Capacity via internal Good Governance
- Leadership & Decision-Making: QQ introduced a structured governance model, formed a dedicated oversight body, and offered capacity building workshops for staff, enhancing advocacy and monitoring capabilities.
- Financial Management: Stricter financial protocols were adopted, along with a new reporting system and external audit mechanisms, ensuring transparency and accountability.
- Monitoring & Research: QQ strengthened its policy research team, improved data collection, and collaborated with academic institutions, enhancing evidence-based advocacy.
Outcome 4: Qëndresa Qytetare lead the National Youth and Students Network in advocacy focused and higher performance of national and regional networks.
- Development of the National Student Congress: In partnership with the European Law Students' Association (ELSA) Albania, QQ successfully organized the National Student Congress on November 15-16, 2024. The congress brought together 120 students from across Albania, with a balanced representation of 60% female and 40% male participants, to discuss challenges within the education system and develop actionable solutions.
- Participation in Regional Forums: QQ representatives, participated in regional forums such as the National Student Forum in North Macedonia and the Congress of Activism in Kosovo. These engagements allowed QQ to present its work, share action plans, and learn from peers in neighboring countries.
Outcome 5: Strengthening Partnership for Environmental Sustainability
Launching TEnjten nQëndresë (Thursdays at Qëndresa). As part of QQ ongoing commitment to sustainability, they organized a series of 20 social and cultural activities focused on sustainable development. These activities engaged 239 participants (33% boys, 64% girls), covering topics such as environmental conservation, waste reduction, sustainable lifestyles, and political activism.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
